display.title: Reb Boruch and the Birth of the Shpoler Zeide
display.summary_short: A generous host welcomes a plain-looking traveler who is really a hidden tzaddik, and is blessed with a son who becomes the Shpoler Zeide.
display.summary_long: Reb Boruch lived up to his name: he gave tzedakah generously, kept a guest house open to every traveler free of charge, and even exchanged his guests' weak horses for strong ones. One bitterly cold Wednesday a simple-looking traveler and his wife arrive, and Reb Boruch begs them to stay for Shabbos. On Friday night a light as bright as the sun shines from the guest's room, where he is saying Tikkun Chatzos. Through the keyhole Reb Boruch sees a second figure dressed in white and faints. The hidden tzaddik reveals that it was the soul of the Maharal of Prague, which is to come down again, and promises Reb Boruch a son with that soul, to be named Aryeh Leib. At the bris the guest blesses the baby to be a 'Zeide', a grandfather to all Israel, and vanishes into the crowd. The nickname stuck. The guest was the Baal Shem Tov, and the child became the famous Shpoler Zeide.
display.lesson: Generous hospitality and tzedakah bring Hashem's blessings.
